results.evidence: In create_saved_metric, normalize_query_for_write(query) is called without existing_uuid, so existing_uuid=None. In normalize_query_for_write: 'if existing_uuid: ... else: normalized_query["uuid"] = str(uuid4())'. Since existing_uuid is always None/falsy for a brand-new metric, the else branch always runs regardless of whether incoming_uuid (caller-supplied) was set, discarding it and generating a fresh uuid4(). The rest of the dict is preserved via 'normalized_query = dict(query)'.

In update_saved_metric: 'existing_uuid = saved_metric.query.get("uuid") if saved_metric.query else None' then 'update_data["query"] = self.normalize_query_for_write(update_data["query"], existing_uuid=existing_uuid)'. Inside normalize_query_for_write, 'if existing_uuid: normalized_query["uuid"] = existing_uuid' preserves the metric's current identifier instead of generating a new one.

'if "saved_metrics_ids" in update_data: ... seen_metric_uuids |= self._collect_saved_metric_uuids(update_data["saved_metrics_ids"])' collects the uuids of shared metrics being linked, then: 'if "metrics" not in update_data and any(metric.get("uuid") in seen_metric_uuids for metric in experiment.metrics or []): update_data["metrics"] = self._assign_uuids_to_metrics(experiment.metrics, seen=seen_metric_uuids)' and the parallel block for metrics_secondary — both compare stored inline metrics against the shared-metric uuids and regenerate on clash, for both primary and secondary collections.

The regeneration only triggers 'if ... any(metric.get("uuid") in seen_metric_uuids ...)'. When no stored inline metric's uuid is in seen_metric_uuids, this condition is False, so update_data["metrics"]/["metrics_secondary"] are never set, leaving the stored inline metrics (and thus their ordering, since ordering sync is driven off update_data keys) completely untouched.

Code comment explains the invariant relied upon: 'the original uuid is kept on the incumbent so any ordering reference to it remains valid... _sync_ordering_with_metric_changes runs later and appends the new regenerated uuids as additions.' This is the same pre-existing ordering mechanism used for the earlier inline/inline clash fix (_assign_uuids_to_metrics), reused here unchanged, so per repository-contract delegation it preserves the original identifier in ordering while adding the new inline identifier.

The clash-resolution block only reassigns update_data["metrics"]/["metrics_secondary"]; it never touches saved_metrics_data or the ExperimentToSavedMetric link-sync code ('saved_metrics_data: list[dict] = update_data.pop("saved_metrics_ids", []) or []'), which is unchanged pre-existing logic that applies the requested link set exactly and leaves the saved metric's own query/uuid untouched.

The updated doc still reads: 'call `experiment-saved-metrics-create` with the same `query` (the `ExperimentMetric` object), attach it via `saved_metrics_ids` as above, **and remove the original entry from the experiment's inline `metrics`/`metrics_secondary` array**...'. This adds the instruction to remove the inline copy, but never instructs omitting the identifier when creating the shared metric — it still says to use 'the same query' object with no mention of stripping the uuid field, so the second half of the criterion is not satisfied.

Pre-existing logic (shown in context, not newly added) populates seen_metric_uuids from current saved-metric links when saved_metrics_ids isn't being updated: 'for link in experiment.experimenttosavedmetric_set... seen_metric_uuids.add(uuid)', and then 'if "metrics" in update_data: update_data["metrics"] = self._assign_uuids_to_metrics(update_data["metrics"], seen=seen_metric_uuids)' regenerates any resent inline metric uuid clashing with an already-linked shared metric, while the shared metric's uuid (and its ordering entry) stays untouched since only the inline list is modified.
